verses.text: The first covenant had rules for worship and an earthly sanctuary.
A tent was set up. In its first room were the lampstand, the table, and the bread set before God. This room was called the Holy Place.
Behind the second curtain was the room called the Most Holy Place.
It contained the gold incense altar and the covenant chest, covered with gold. Inside were a gold jar of manna, Aaron's staff that had budded, and the covenant tablets.
Above the chest were the glorious cherubim overshadowing the place of atonement. We can't discuss these things in detail now.
With everything arranged this way, the priests regularly entered the first room to carry out their service.
But only the high priest entered the second room, and only once a year, bringing blood to offer for himself and for the people's sins committed in ignorance.
By this, the Holy Spirit was showing that the way into the Most Holy Place wasn't yet open as long as the first tent was still standing.
This is an illustration for the present time. Gifts and sacrifices are offered, but they can't make the worshiper's conscience clear.
They deal only with food and drink and various ritual washings—outward rules that last until the time of renewal.
But when Christ came as high priest of the good things now here, he went through the greater and more perfect tent, not made by human hands and not part of this creation.
He didn't enter by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood, entering the Most Holy Place once for all and securing eternal redemption.
If the blood of goats and bulls and the ashes of a heifer sprinkled on those who are ceremonially unclean can make their bodies clean,
how much more will Christ's blood cleanse our consciences from useless deeds so we can serve the living God? Through the eternal Spirit, Christ offered himself to God without blemish.

That's why Christ is the mediator of a new covenant. A death has taken place to set people free from the sins committed under the first covenant, so those who are called may receive the promised eternal inheritance.
Where there is a will, the death of the one who made it must be established.
A will takes effect only after someone has died; it has no force while the person who made it is still alive.
That's why even the first covenant wasn't put into effect without blood.
After Moses had announced every commandment to all the people, he took the blood of calves and goats, along with water, scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled the scroll and all the people.
He said, ‘This is the blood of the covenant God commanded you to keep.’
In the same way, he sprinkled the tent and all the objects used in worship with blood.
According to the law, almost everything is cleansed with blood, and without blood being shed there is no forgiveness.
So the copies of the heavenly things had to be cleansed with these sacrifices, but the heavenly things themselves required better sacrifices.
Christ didn't enter a holy place made by human hands, which is only a copy of the true one. He entered heaven itself, and now appears in God's presence for us.
He didn't enter heaven to offer himself over and over, the way the high priest enters the Most Holy Place every year with blood that isn't his own.
Otherwise, Christ would have had to suffer again and again since the world began. Instead, he has appeared once at the culmination of the ages to remove sin by offering himself.
People are appointed to die once, and after that to face judgment.
In the same way, Christ was offered once to carry the sins of many. He will appear a second time—not to deal with sin, but to save those who are waiting eagerly for him.
